statements.statement: MongoDB process resident memory excludes other processes on the node.
Atlas system memory and the projected memory used for scale-down are different quantities, so the resident-memory chart cannot substitute for the target-tier memory calculation.
statements.note: The auto-scaling page defines projected memory as distinct from system memory; it is computed from System Memory Used and tier cache sizes, not from resident memory. The conclusion about the resident chart is inferred.

edits.rationale: The metrics page says memory_resident counts only the MongoDB process. The Atlas Core auto-scaling page says scale-down uses Projected Memory Utilization, built from System Memory Used with the WiredTiger cache swapped for 80% of the new tier's cache, and that this differs from System Memory Utilization. Projected memory therefore cannot be read off the resident-memory chart. That last step is a direct inference from the two pages, not a sentence either page states.

edits.old: Efficient query and index design can reduce memory demand and help avoid a higher instance tier; resource demand should be reviewed after tuning as part of the sizing decision. (medium confidence)
edits.new: Managing schemas and indexes efficiently can reduce memory consumption and help avoid a higher instance tier. Sources: https://community.ibm.com/community/user/blogs/manish-negandhi/2026/04/14/optimizing-mongodb-atlas-cost

evidence.quote: Managing schemas and index efficiently will result in less memory consumption and therefore avoiding higher instance tier usage

The working set is the sum of all the indexes plus the set of documents that are accessed frequently. If your working set fits in RAM, then MongoDB can serve queries from memory, which provides the fastest query response times.

edits.old: Use several resource dimensions to assess a smaller Atlas tier: CPU, memory and WiredTiger cache, disk IOPS, connections, and workload latency. Low CPU alone does not establish that the smaller tier will satisfy the workload. (high confidence)
edits.new: To assess a move to a lower Atlas tier, monitor the cluster's CPU, WiredTiger cache, memory and IOPS over a rolling 30-day period of normal use; Atlas generally recommends scaling down if usage is steadily below 45% of allocated resources. Also monitor connections against the current connection limits. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics/

edits.old: Cache fill measures occupied cache bytes divided by configured cache bytes; it is not a cache-hit percentage. Review cache reads from disk, disk IOPS versus provisioned limits, and disk latency alongside cache occupancy when judging memory pressure. (high confidence)
edits.new: Cache fill ratio is calculated by dividing the number of bytes currently in the cache by the maximum number of bytes configured, as a percentage. Alongside it, review cache activity (data read from disk into memory), disk IOPS against the maximum provisioned IOPS, and disk latency. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-available-metrics/
